NASB.1: The LORD spoke again to Moses and to Aaron, saying to them,
NASB.2: 'Speak to the sons of Israel, saying, 'These are the creatures which you may eat from all the animals that are on the earth.
NASB.3: 'Whatever divides a hoof, thus making split hoofs, [and] chews the cud, among the animals, that you may eat.
NASB.4: 'Nevertheless, you are not to eat of these, among those which chew the cud, or among those which divide the hoof: the camel, for though it chews cud, it does not divide the hoof, it is unclean to you.
NASB.5: 'Likewise, the shaphan, for though it chews cud, it does not divide the hoof, it is unclean to you;
NASB.6: the rabbit also, for though it chews cud, it does not divide the hoof, it is unclean to you;
NASB.7: and the pig, for though it divides the hoof, thus making a split hoof, it does not chew cud, it is unclean to you.
NASB.8: 'You shall not eat of their flesh nor touch their carcasses; they are unclean to you.
NASB.9: 'These you may eat, whatever is in the water: all that have fins and scales, those in the water, in the seas or in the rivers, you may eat.
NASB.10: 'But whatever is in the seas and in the rivers that does not have fins and scales among all the teeming life of the water, and among all the living creatures that are in the water, they are detestable things to you,
NASB.11: and they shall be abhorrent to you; you may not eat of their flesh, and their carcasses you shall detest.
NASB.12: 'Whatever in the water does not have fins and scales is abhorrent to you.
NASB.13: 'These, moreover, you shall detest among the birds; they are abhorrent, not to be eaten: the eagle and the vulture and the buzzard,
NASB.14: and the kite and the falcon in its kind,
NASB.16: and the ostrich and the owl and the sea gull and the hawk in its kind,
NASB.17: and the little owl and the cormorant and the great owl,
NASB.18: and the white owl and the pelican and the carrion vulture,
NASB.19: and the stork, the heron in its kinds, and the hoopoe, and the bat.
NASB.20: 'All the winged insects that walk on [all] fours are detestable to you.
NASB.21: 'Yet these you may eat among all the winged insects which walk on [all] fours: those which have above their feet jointed legs with which to jump on the earth.
NASB.22: 'These of them you may eat: the locust in its kinds, and the devastating locust in its kinds, and the cricket in its kinds, and the grasshopper in its kinds.
NASB.23: 'But all other winged insects which are four-footed are detestable to you.
NASB.24: 'By these, moreover, you will be made unclean: whoever touches their carcasses becomes unclean until evening,
NASB.25: and whoever picks up any of their carcasses shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening.
NASB.26: 'Concerning all the animals which divide the hoof but do not make a split [hoof], or which do not chew cud, they are unclean to you: whoever touches them becomes unclean.
NASB.27: 'Also whatever walks on its paws, among all the creatures that walk on [all] fours, are unclean to you; whoever touches their carcasses becomes unclean until evening,
NASB.28: and the one who picks up their carcasses shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening; they are unclean to you.
NASB.29: 'Now these are to you the unclean among the swarming things which swarm on the earth: the mole, and the mouse, and the great lizard in its kinds,
NASB.30: and the gecko, and the crocodile, and the lizard, and the sand reptile, and the chameleon.
NASB.31: 'These are to you the unclean among all the swarming things; whoever touches them when they are dead becomes unclean until evening.
NASB.32: 'Also anything on which one of them may fall when they are dead becomes unclean, including any wooden article, or clothing, or a skin, or a sack-- any article of which use is made-- it shall be put in the water and be unclean until evening, then it becomes clean.
NASB.33: 'As for any earthenware vessel into which one of them may fall, whatever is in it becomes unclean and you shall break the vessel.
NASB.34: 'Any of the food which may be eaten, on which water comes, shall become unclean, and any liquid which may be drunk in every vessel shall become unclean.
NASB.35: 'Everything, moreover, on which part of their carcass may fall becomes unclean; an oven or a stove shall be smashed; they are unclean and shall continue as unclean to you.
NASB.36: 'Nevertheless a spring or a cistern collecting water shall be clean, though the one who touches their carcass shall be unclean.
NASB.37: 'If a part of their carcass falls on any seed for sowing which is to be sown, it is clean.
NASB.38: 'Though if water is put on the seed and a part of their carcass falls on it, it is unclean to you.
NASB.39: 'Also if one of the animals dies which you have for food, the one who touches its carcass becomes unclean until evening.
NASB.40: 'He too, who eats some of its carcass shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening, and the one who picks up its carcass shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening.
NASB.41: 'Now every swarming thing that swarms on the earth is detestable, not to be eaten.
NASB.42: 'Whatever crawls on its belly, and whatever walks on [all] fours, whatever has many feet, in respect to every swarming thing that swarms on the earth, you shall not eat them, for they are detestable.
NASB.43: 'Do not render yourselves detestable through any of the swarming things that swarm; and you shall not make yourselves unclean with them so that you become unclean.
NASB.44: 'For I am the LORD your God. Consecrate yourselves therefore, and be holy, for I am holy. And you shall not make yourselves unclean with any of the swarming things that swarm on the earth.
NASB.45: 'For I am the LORD who brought you up from the land of Egypt to be your God; thus you shall be holy, for I am holy.''
NASB.46: This is the law regarding the animal and the bird, and every living thing that moves in the waters and everything that swarms on the earth,
NASB.47: to make a distinction between the unclean and the clean, and between the edible creature and the creature which is not to be eaten.

ESV.1: And the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying to them,
ESV.2: “Speak to the people of Israel, saying, These are the living things that you may eat among all the animals that are on the earth.
ESV.3: Whatever parts the hoof and is cloven-footed and chews the cud, among the animals, you may eat.
ESV.4: Nevertheless, among those that chew the cud or part the hoof, you shall not eat these: The camel, because it chews the cud but does not part the hoof, is unclean to you.
ESV.5: And the rock badger, because it chews the cud but does not part the hoof, is unclean to you.
ESV.6: And the hare, because it chews the cud but does not part the hoof, is unclean to you.
ESV.7: And the pig, because it parts the hoof and is cloven-footed but does not chew the cud, is unclean to you.
ESV.8: You shall not eat any of their flesh, and you shall not touch their carcasses; they are unclean to you.
ESV.9: “These you may eat, of all that are in the waters. Everything in the waters that has fins and scales, whether in the seas or in the rivers, you may eat.
ESV.10: But anything in the seas or the rivers that does not have fins and scales, of the swarming creatures in the waters and of the living creatures that are in the waters, is detestable to you.
ESV.11: You shall regard them as detestable; you shall not eat any of their flesh, and you shall detest their carcasses.
ESV.12: Everything in the waters that does not have fins and scales is detestable to you.
ESV.13: “And these you shall detest among the birds;  they shall not be eaten; they are detestable: the eagle,  the bearded vulture, the black vulture,
ESV.14: the kite, the falcon of any kind,
ESV.16: the ostrich, the nighthawk, the sea gull, the hawk of any kind,
ESV.17: the little owl, the cormorant, the short-eared owl,
ESV.18: the barn owl, the tawny owl, the carrion vulture,
ESV.19: the stork, the heron of any kind, the hoopoe, and the bat.
ESV.20: “All winged insects that go on all fours are detestable to you.
ESV.21: Yet among the winged insects that go on all fours you may eat those that have jointed legs above their feet, with which to hop on the ground.
ESV.22: Of them you may eat: the locust of any kind, the bald locust of any kind, the cricket of any kind, and the grasshopper of any kind.
ESV.23: But all other winged insects that have four feet are detestable to you.
ESV.24: “And by these you shall become unclean. Whoever touches their carcass shall be unclean until the evening,
ESV.25: and whoever carries any part of their carcass shall wash his clothes and be unclean until the evening.
ESV.26: Every animal that parts the hoof but is not cloven-footed or does not chew the cud is unclean to you. Everyone who touches them shall be unclean.
ESV.27: And all that walk on their paws, among the animals that go on all fours, are unclean to you. Whoever touches their carcass shall be unclean until the evening,
ESV.28: and he who carries their carcass shall wash his clothes and be unclean until the evening; they are unclean to you.
ESV.29: “And these are unclean to you among the swarming things that swarm on the ground: the mole rat, the mouse, the great lizard of any kind,
ESV.30: the gecko, the monitor lizard, the lizard, the sand lizard, and the chameleon.
ESV.31: These are unclean to you among all that swarm. Whoever touches them when they are dead shall be unclean until the evening.
ESV.32: And anything on which any of them falls when they are dead shall be unclean, whether it is an article of wood or a garment or a skin or a sack, any article that is used for any purpose. It must be put into water, and it shall be unclean until the evening; then it shall be clean.
ESV.33: And if any of them falls into any earthenware vessel, all that is in it shall be unclean, and you shall break it.
ESV.34: Any food in it that could be eaten, on which water comes, shall be unclean. And all drink that could be drunk from every such vessel shall be unclean.
ESV.35: And everything on which any part of their carcass falls shall be unclean. Whether oven or stove, it shall be broken in pieces. They are unclean and shall remain unclean for you.
ESV.36: Nevertheless, a spring or a cistern holding water shall be clean, but whoever touches a carcass in them shall be unclean.
ESV.37: And if any part of their carcass falls upon any seed grain that is to be sown, it is clean,
ESV.38: but if water is put on the seed and any part of their carcass falls on it, it is unclean to you.
ESV.39: “And if any animal which you may eat dies, whoever touches its carcass shall be unclean until the evening,
ESV.40: and whoever eats of its carcass shall wash his clothes and be unclean until the evening. And whoever carries the carcass shall wash his clothes and be unclean until the evening.
ESV.41: “Every swarming thing that swarms on the ground is detestable; it shall not be eaten.
ESV.42: Whatever goes on its belly, and whatever goes on all fours, or whatever has many feet, any swarming thing that swarms on the ground, you shall not eat, for they are detestable.
ESV.43: You shall not make yourselves detestable with any swarming thing that swarms, and you shall not defile yourselves with them, and become unclean through them.
ESV.44: For I am the LORD your God. Consecrate yourselves therefore, and be holy, for I am holy. You shall not defile yourselves with any swarming thing that crawls on the ground.
ESV.45: For I am the LORD who brought you up out of the land of Egypt to be your God. You shall therefore be holy, for I am holy.”
ESV.46: This is the law about beast and bird and every living creature that moves through the waters and every creature that swarms on the ground,
ESV.47: to make a distinction between the unclean and the clean and between the living creature that may be eaten and the living creature that may not be eaten.

NKJV.10: But all in the seas or in the rivers that do not have fins and scales, all that move in the water or any living thing which is in the water, they are an abomination to you.
NKJV.11: They shall be an abomination to you; you shall not eat their flesh, but you shall regard their carcasses as an abomination.
NKJV.12: Whatever in the water does not have fins or scales—that shall be an abomination to you.
NKJV.13: ‘And these you shall regard as an abomination among the birds; they shall not be eaten, they are an abomination: the eagle, the vulture, the buzzard,
NKJV.14: the kite, and the falcon after its kind;
NKJV.16: the ostrich, the short-eared owl, the sea gull, and the hawk after its kind;
NKJV.17: the little owl, the fisher owl, and the screech owl;
NKJV.18: the white owl, the jackdaw, and the carrion vulture;
NKJV.19: the stork, the heron after its kind, the hoopoe, and the bat.
NKJV.20: ‘All flying insects that creep on all fours shall be an abomination to you.
NKJV.21: Yet these you may eat of every flying insect that creeps on all fours: those which have jointed legs above their feet with which to leap on the earth.
NKJV.22: These you may eat: the locust after its kind, the destroying locust after its kind, the cricket after its kind, and the grasshopper after its kind.
NKJV.23: But all other flying insects which have four feet shall be an abomination to you.
NKJV.24: ‘By these you shall become unclean; whoever touches the carcass of any of them shall be unclean until evening;
NKJV.25: whoever carries part of the carcass of any of them shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening:
NKJV.26: The carcass of any animal which divides the foot, but is not cloven-hoofed or does not chew the cud, is unclean to you. Everyone who touches it shall be unclean.
NKJV.27: And whatever goes on its paws, among all kinds of animals that go on all fours, those are unclean to you. Whoever touches any such carcass shall be unclean until evening.
NKJV.28: Whoever carries any such carcass shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening. It is unclean to you.
NKJV.29: ‘These also shall be unclean to you among the creeping things that creep on the earth: the mole, the mouse, and the large lizard after its kind;
NKJV.30: the gecko, the monitor lizard, the sand reptile, the sand lizard, and the chameleon.
NKJV.31: These are unclean to you among all that creep. Whoever touches them when they are dead shall be unclean until evening.
NKJV.32: Anything on which any of them falls, when they are dead shall be unclean, whether it is any item of wood or clothing or skin or sack, whatever item it is, in which any work is done, it must be put in water. And it shall be unclean until evening; then it shall be clean.
NKJV.33: Any earthen vessel into which any of them falls you shall break; and whatever is in it shall be unclean:
NKJV.34: in such a vessel, any edible food upon which water falls becomes unclean, and any drink that may be drunk from it becomes unclean.
NKJV.35: And everything on which a part of any such carcass falls shall be unclean; whether it is an oven or cooking stove, it shall be broken down; for they are unclean, and shall be unclean to you.
NKJV.36: Nevertheless a spring or a cistern, in which there is plenty of water, shall be clean, but whatever touches any such carcass becomes unclean.
NKJV.37: And if a part of any such carcass falls on any planting seed which is to be sown, it remains clean.
NKJV.38: But if water is put on the seed, and if a part of any such carcass falls on it, it becomes unclean to you.
NKJV.39: ‘And if any animal which you may eat dies, he who touches its carcass shall be unclean until evening.
NKJV.40: He who eats of its carcass shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening. He also who carries its carcass shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening.
NKJV.41: ‘And every creeping thing that creeps on the earth shall be an abomination. It shall not be eaten.
NKJV.42: Whatever crawls on its belly, whatever goes on all fours, or whatever has many feet among all creeping things that creep on the earth—these you shall not eat, for they are an abomination.
NKJV.43: You shall not make yourselves abominable with any creeping thing that creeps; nor shall you make yourselves unclean with them, lest you be defiled by them.
NKJV.44: For I am the LORD your God. You shall therefore consecrate yourselves, and you shall be holy; for I am holy. Neither shall you defile yourselves with any creeping thing that creeps on the earth.
NKJV.45: For I am the LORD who brings you up out of the land of Egypt, to be your God. You shall therefore be holy, for I am holy.
NKJV.46: ‘This is the law of the animals and the birds and every living creature that moves in the waters, and of every creature that creeps on the earth,
NKJV.47: to distinguish between the unclean and the clean, and between the animal that may be eaten and the animal that may not be eaten.’ ”

WEB.1: Yahweh spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying to them,
WEB.2: “Speak to the children of Israel, saying, ‘These are the living things which you may eat among all the animals that are on the earth.
WEB.3: Whatever parts the hoof, and is cloven-footed, and chews the cud among the animals, that you may eat.
WEB.4: “‘Nevertheless these you shall not eat of those that chew the cud, or of those who part the hoof: the camel, because he chews the cud but doesn’t have a parted hoof, he is unclean to you.
WEB.5: The cony,  because he chews the cud but doesn’t have a parted hoof, he is unclean to you.
WEB.6: The hare, because she chews the cud but doesn’t part the hoof, she is unclean to you.
WEB.7: The pig, because he has a split hoof, and is cloven-footed, but doesn’t chew the cud, he is unclean to you.
WEB.8: Of their meat you shall not eat, and their carcasses you shall not touch; they are unclean to you.
WEB.9: “‘These you may eat of all that are in the waters: whatever has fins and scales in the waters, in the seas, and in the rivers, that you may eat.
WEB.10: All that don’t have fins and scales in the seas, and in the rivers, of all that move in the waters, and of all the living creatures that are in the waters, they are an abomination to you,
WEB.11: and you detest them. You shall not eat of their meat, and you shall detest their carcasses.
WEB.12: Whatever has no fins nor scales in the waters, that is an abomination to you.
WEB.13: “‘These you shall detest among the birds; they shall not be eaten, they are an abomination: the eagle, and the vulture, and the black vulture,
WEB.14: and the red kite, any kind of black kite,
WEB.16: the horned owl, the screech owl, and the gull, any kind of hawk,
WEB.17: the little owl, the cormorant, the great owl,
WEB.18: the white owl, the desert owl, the osprey,
WEB.19: the stork, any kind of heron, the hoopoe, and the bat.
WEB.20: “‘All flying insects that walk on all fours are an abomination to you.
WEB.21: Yet you may eat these: of all winged creeping things that go on all fours, which have legs above their feet, with which to hop on the earth.
WEB.22: Even of these you may eat: any kind of locust, any kind of katydid, any kind of cricket, and any kind of grasshopper.
WEB.23: But all winged creeping things which have four feet, are an abomination to you.
WEB.24: “‘By these you will become unclean: whoever touches their carcass shall be unclean until the evening.
WEB.25: Whoever carries any part of their carcass shall wash his clothes, and be unclean until the evening.
WEB.26: “‘Every animal which parts the hoof, and is not cloven-footed, nor chews the cud, is unclean to you. Everyone who touches them shall be unclean.
WEB.27: Whatever goes on its paws, among all animals that go on all fours, they are unclean to you. Whoever touches their carcass shall be unclean until the evening.
WEB.28: He who carries their carcass shall wash his clothes, and be unclean until the evening. They are unclean to you.
WEB.29: “‘These are they which are unclean to you among the creeping things that creep on the earth: the weasel, the rat, any kind of great lizard,
WEB.30: the gecko, and the monitor lizard, the wall lizard, the skink, and the chameleon.
WEB.31: These are they which are unclean to you among all that creep. Whoever touches them when they are dead, shall be unclean until the evening.
WEB.32: On whatever any of them falls when they are dead, it shall be unclean; whether it is any vessel of wood, or clothing, or skin, or sack, whatever vessel it is, with which any work is done, it must be put into water, and it shall be unclean until the evening; then it will be clean.
WEB.33: Every earthen vessel, into which any of them falls, all that is in it shall be unclean, and you shall break it.
WEB.34: All food which may be eaten, that on which water comes, shall be unclean; and all drink that may be drunk in every such vessel shall be unclean.
WEB.35: Everything whereupon part of their carcass falls shall be unclean; whether oven, or range for pots, it shall be broken in pieces: they are unclean, and shall be unclean to you.
WEB.36: Nevertheless a spring or a cistern in which water is gathered shall be clean: but that which touches their carcass shall be unclean.
WEB.37: If part of their carcass falls on any sowing seed which is to be sown, it is clean.
WEB.38: But if water is put on the seed, and part of their carcass falls on it, it is unclean to you.
WEB.39: “‘If any animal, of which you may eat, dies; he who touches its carcass shall be unclean until the evening.
WEB.40: He who eats of its carcass shall wash his clothes, and be unclean until the evening. He also who carries its carcass shall wash his clothes, and be unclean until the evening.
WEB.41: “‘Every creeping thing that creeps on the earth is an abomination. It shall not be eaten.
WEB.42: Whatever goes on its belly, and whatever goes on all fours, or whatever has many feet, even all creeping things that creep on the earth, them you shall not eat; for they are an abomination.
WEB.43: You shall not make yourselves abominable with any creeping thing that creeps. You shall not make yourselves unclean with them, that you should be defiled thereby.
WEB.44: For I am Yahweh your God. Sanctify yourselves therefore, and be holy; for I am holy. You shall not defile yourselves with any kind of creeping thing that moves on the earth.
WEB.45: For I am Yahweh who brought you up out of the land of Egypt, to be your God. You shall therefore be holy, for I am holy.
WEB.46: “‘This is the law of the animal, and of the bird, and of every living creature that moves in the waters, and of every creature that creeps on the earth,
WEB.47: to make a distinction between the unclean and the clean, and between the living thing that may be eaten and the living thing that may not be eaten.’”

CSB17.6: hares, though they chew the cud, do not have hooves — they are unclean for you;
CSB17.7: pigs, though they have divided hooves, do not chew the cud — they are unclean for you.
CSB17.8: Do not eat any of their meat or touch their carcasses — they are unclean for you. <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.9: “This is what you may eat from all that is in the water: You may eat everything in the water that has fins and scales, whether in the seas or streams.
CSB17.10: But these are to be abhorrent to you: everything in the seas or streams that does not have fins and scales among all the swarming things and other living creatures <sup>ⓔ</sup> in the water.
CSB17.11: They are to remain abhorrent to you; you must not eat any of their meat, and you must abhor their carcasses.
CSB17.12: Everything in the water that does not have fins and scales will be abhorrent to you.

CSB17.22: You may eat these: any kind of locust, ⓚ katydid, cricket, and grasshopper.

NLT.1: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
NLT.2: “Give the following instructions to the people of Israel. “Of all the land animals, these are the ones you may use for food.
NLT.3: You may eat any animal that has completely split hooves and chews the cud.
NLT.4: You may not, however, eat the following animals that have split hooves or that chew the cud, but not both. The camel chews the cud but does not have split hooves, so it is ceremonially unclean for you.
NLT.5: The hyrax chews the cud but does not have split hooves, so it is unclean.
NLT.6: The hare chews the cud but does not have split hooves, so it is unclean.
NLT.7: The pig has evenly split hooves but does not chew the cud, so it is unclean.
NLT.8: You may not eat the meat of these animals or even touch their carcasses. They are ceremonially unclean for you.
NLT.9: “Of all the marine animals, these are ones you may use for food. You may eat anything from the water if it has both fins and scales, whether taken from salt water or from streams.
NLT.10: But you must never eat animals from the sea or from rivers that do not have both fins and scales. They are detestable to you. This applies both to little creatures that live in shallow water and to all creatures that live in deep water.
NLT.11: They will always be detestable to you. You must never eat their meat or even touch their dead bodies.
NLT.12: Any marine animal that does not have both fins and scales is detestable to you.
NLT.13: “These are the birds that are detestable to you. You must never eat them: the griffon vulture, the bearded vulture, the black vulture,
NLT.14: the kite, falcons of all kinds,
NLT.16: the eagle owl, the short-eared owl, the seagull, hawks of all kinds,
NLT.17: the little owl, the cormorant, the great owl,
NLT.18: the barn owl, the desert owl, the Egyptian vulture,
NLT.19: the stork, herons of all kinds, the hoopoe, and the bat.
NLT.20: “You must not eat winged insects that walk along the ground; they are detestable to you.
NLT.21: You may, however, eat winged insects that walk along the ground and have jointed legs so they can jump.
NLT.22: The insects you are permitted to eat include all kinds of locusts, bald locusts, crickets, and grasshoppers.
NLT.23: All other winged insects that walk along the ground are detestable to you.
NLT.24: “The following creatures will make you ceremonially unclean. If any of you touch their carcasses, you will be defiled until evening.
NLT.25: If you pick up their carcasses, you must wash your clothes, and you will remain defiled until evening.
NLT.26: “Any animal that has split hooves that are not evenly divided or that does not chew the cud is unclean for you. If you touch the carcass of such an animal, you will be defiled.
NLT.27: Of the animals that walk on all fours, those that have paws are unclean. If you touch the carcass of such an animal, you will be defiled until evening.
NLT.28: If you pick up its carcass, you must wash your clothes, and you will remain defiled until evening. These animals are unclean for you.
NLT.29: “Of the small animals that scurry along the ground, these are unclean for you: the mole rat, the rat, large lizards of all kinds,
NLT.30: the gecko, the monitor lizard, the common lizard, the sand lizard, and the chameleon.
NLT.31: All these small animals are unclean for you. If any of you touch the dead body of such an animal, you will be defiled until evening.
NLT.32: If such an animal dies and falls on something, that object will be unclean. This is true whether the object is made of wood, cloth, leather, or burlap. Whatever its use, you must dip it in water, and it will remain defiled until evening. After that, it will be ceremonially clean and may be used again.
NLT.33: “If such an animal falls into a clay pot, everything in the pot will be defiled, and the pot must be smashed.
NLT.34: If the water from such a container spills on any food, the food will be defiled. And any beverage in such a container will be defiled.
NLT.35: Any object on which the carcass of such an animal falls will be defiled. If it is an oven or hearth, it must be destroyed, for it is defiled, and you must treat it accordingly.
NLT.36: “However, if the carcass of such an animal falls into a spring or a cistern, the water will still be clean. But anyone who touches the carcass will be defiled.
NLT.37: If the carcass falls on seed grain to be planted in the field, the seed will still be considered clean.
NLT.38: But if the seed is wet when the carcass falls on it, the seed will be defiled.
NLT.39: “If an animal you are permitted to eat dies and you touch its carcass, you will be defiled until evening.
NLT.40: If you eat any of its meat or carry away its carcass, you must wash your clothes, and you will remain defiled until evening.
NLT.41: “All small animals that scurry along the ground are detestable, and you must never eat them.
NLT.42: This includes all animals that slither along on their bellies, as well as those with four legs and those with many feet. All such animals that scurry along the ground are detestable, and you must never eat them.
NLT.43: Do not defile yourselves by touching them. You must not make yourselves ceremonially unclean because of them.
NLT.44: For I am the LORD your God. You must consecrate yourselves and be holy, because I am holy. So do not defile yourselves with any of these small animals that scurry along the ground.
NLT.45: For I, the LORD, am the one who brought you up from the land of Egypt, that I might be your God. Therefore, you must be holy because I am holy.
NLT.46: “These are the instructions regarding land animals, birds, marine creatures, and animals that scurry along the ground.
NLT.47: By these instructions you will know what is unclean and clean, and which animals may be eaten and which may not be eaten.”

AMP.1: The LORD spoke again to Moses and Aaron, saying to them,
AMP.2: "Speak to the children of Israel, saying, 'Among all the animals which are on the earth, these are the animals which you may eat.
AMP.3: You may eat any animal that has a divided hoof [that is, a hoof split into two parts especially at its distal extremity] and chews the cud.
AMP.4: Nevertheless, you are not to eat these, among those which chew the cud or divide the hoof: the camel, because it chews the cud but does not divide the hoof; it is [ceremonially] unclean to you.
AMP.5: And the shaphan, because it chews the cud but does not divide the hoof; it is unclean to you.
AMP.6: And the hare, because it chews the cud but does not divide the hoof; it is unclean to you.
AMP.7: And the swine, because it divides the hoof and makes a split hoof, but does not chew the cud; it is unclean to you.
AMP.8: You shall not eat their meat nor touch their carcasses; they are unclean to you.
AMP.9: 'These you may eat, whatever is in the water: whatever has fins and scales in the waters, in the seas, and in the rivers, these you may eat;
AMP.10: but whatever does not have fins and scales in the seas and in the rivers, of all the teeming life in the waters, and of all the living creatures that are in the waters, they are [to be considered] detestable to you.
AMP.11: They shall be hated things to you. You may not eat their meat; you shall detest their carcasses.
AMP.12: Everything in the water that does not have fins and scales is detestable to you.
AMP.13: 'These you shall detest among the birds; they are not to be eaten, for they are hated things: the eagle and the vulture and the buzzard,
AMP.14: the kite, every kind of falcon,
AMP.16: the ostrich, the nighthawk, the sea gull, every species of hawk,
AMP.17: the little owl and the cormorant and the great owl,
AMP.18: the white owl, the pelican, the carrion vulture,
AMP.19: the stork, all kinds of heron, the hoopoe, and the bat.
AMP.20: 'All winged insects that walk on all fours are detestable to you;
AMP.21: yet of all winged insects that walk on all fours you may eat those which have legs above their feet with which to leap on the ground.
AMP.22: Of these you may eat: the whole species of migratory locust, of bald locust, of cricket, and of grasshopper.
AMP.23: But all other winged insects which are four footed are detestable to you.
AMP.24: 'By [contact with] these you will become unclean; whoever touches their carcasses becomes unclean until the evening (dusk),
AMP.25: and whoever picks up any of their carcasses shall wash his clothes and be unclean until the evening.
AMP.26: Concerning all the animals which divide the hoof, but do not have a split hoof, or which do not chew the cud, they are unclean to you; whoever touches them becomes unclean.
AMP.27: Also all animals that walk on their paws, among all kinds of animals that walk on four legs, are unclean to you; whoever touches their carcasses becomes unclean until the evening,
AMP.28: and the one who picks up their carcasses shall wash his clothes and be unclean until the evening; they are unclean to you.
AMP.29: 'These also are unclean to you among the swarming things that crawl around on the ground [and multiply profusely]: the mole, the mouse, and any kind of great lizard,
AMP.30: the gecko, the crocodile, the lizard, the sand reptile, and the chameleon.
AMP.31: These [creatures] are unclean to you among all that swarm; whoever touches them when they are dead becomes unclean until evening.
AMP.32: Also anything on which one of them falls after dying becomes unclean, whether it is an article of wood or clothing, or a skin, or a sack—any article that is used—it must be put in water, and will be unclean until the evening; then it becomes clean.
AMP.33: As for any earthenware container into which any of these [crawling things] falls, whatever is in it becomes unclean, and you shall break the container.
AMP.34: Any of the food which may be eaten, but on which [unclean] water falls, shall become unclean, and any liquid that may be drunk in every container shall become unclean.
AMP.35: Everything that part of their carcass falls on becomes unclean; an oven, or a small stove shall be smashed; they are unclean, and shall be unclean to you.
AMP.36: Nevertheless a spring or a cistern (reservoir) collecting water shall be clean; but whoever touches one of these carcasses shall be unclean.
AMP.37: If a part of their carcass falls on any seed for sowing which is to be sown, it is clean;
AMP.38: but if water is put on the seed and a part of their carcass falls on it, it is unclean to you.
AMP.39: 'If one of the animals that you may eat dies [of natural causes], whoever touches its carcass becomes unclean until the evening.
AMP.40: And whoever eats some of its meat shall wash his clothes, and be unclean until evening; also whoever picks up its carcass shall wash his clothes, and be unclean until the evening.
AMP.41: 'Now everything that swarms on the ground is detestable; it is not to be eaten.
AMP.42: Whatever crawls on its belly, and whatever walks on all fours, and whatever has many feet among all things that swarm on the ground, you shall not eat; for they are detestable.
AMP.43: Do not make yourselves loathsome (impure, repulsive) by [eating] any swarming thing; you shall not make yourselves unclean by them so as to defile yourselves.

AMP.45: For I am the LORD who brought you up from the land of Egypt to be your God; therefore you shall be holy, for I am holy.'"

NIV.1:
Clean and Unclean Food
The Lord said to Moses and Aaron,
NIV.2: “Say to the Israelites: ‘Of all the animals that live on land, these are the ones you may eat:
NIV.3: You may eat any animal that has a split hoof completely divided and that chews the cud.
NIV.4: “‘There are some that only chew the cud or only have a split hoof, but you must not eat them. The camel, though it chews the cud, does not have a split hoof; it is ceremonially unclean for you.
NIV.5: The coney, though it chews the cud, does not have a split hoof; it is unclean for you.
NIV.6: The rabbit, though it chews the cud, does not have a split hoof; it is unclean for you.
NIV.7: And the pig, though it has a split hoof completely divided, does not chew the cud; it is unclean for you.
NIV.8: You must not eat their meat or touch their carcasses; they are unclean for you.
NIV.9: “‘Of all the creatures living in the water of the seas and the streams, you may eat any that have fins and scales.
NIV.10: But all creatures in the seas or streams that do not have fins and scales—whether among all the swarming things or among all the other living creatures in the water—you are to detest.
NIV.11: And since you are to detest them, you must not eat their meat and you must detest their carcasses.
NIV.12: Anything living in the water that does not have fins and scales is to be detestable to you.
NIV.13: “‘These are the birds you are to detest and not eat because they are detestable: the eagle, the vulture, the black vulture,
NIV.14: the red kite, any kind of black kite,
NIV.16: the horned owl, the screech owl, the gull, any kind of hawk,
NIV.17: the little owl, the cormorant, the great owl,
NIV.18: the white owl, the desert owl, the osprey,
NIV.19: the stork, any kind of heron, the hoopoe and the bat.
NIV.20: “‘All flying insects that walk on all fours are to be detestable to you.
NIV.21: There are, however, some winged creatures that walk on all fours that you may eat: those that have jointed legs for hopping on the ground.
NIV.22: Of these you may eat any kind of locust, katydid, cricket or grasshopper.
NIV.23: But all other winged creatures that have four legs you are to detest.
NIV.24: “‘You will make yourselves unclean by these; whoever touches their carcasses will be unclean till evening.
NIV.25: Whoever picks up one of their carcasses must wash his clothes, and he will be unclean till evening.
NIV.26: “‘Every animal that has a split hoof not completely divided or that does not chew the cud is unclean for you; whoever touches the carcass of any of them will be unclean.
NIV.27: Of all the animals that walk on all fours, those that walk on their paws are unclean for you; whoever touches their carcasses will be unclean till evening.
NIV.28: Anyone who picks up their carcasses must wash his clothes, and he will be unclean till evening. They are unclean for you.
NIV.29: “‘Of the animals that move about on the ground, these are unclean for you: the weasel, the rat, any kind of great lizard,
NIV.30: the gecko, the monitor lizard, the wall lizard, the skink and the chameleon.
NIV.31: Of all those that move along the ground, these are unclean for you. Whoever touches them when they are dead will be unclean till evening.
NIV.32: When one of them dies and falls on something, that article, whatever its use, will be unclean, whether it is made of wood, cloth, hide or sackcloth. Put it in water; it will be unclean till evening, and then it will be clean.
NIV.33: If one of them falls into a clay pot, everything in it will be unclean, and you must break the pot.
NIV.34: Any food that could be eaten but has water on it from such a pot is unclean, and any liquid that could be drunk from it is unclean.
NIV.35: Anything that one of their carcasses falls on becomes unclean; an oven or cooking pot must be broken up. They are unclean, and you are to regard them as unclean.
NIV.36: A spring, however, or a cistern for collecting water remains clean, but anyone who touches one of these carcasses is unclean.
NIV.37: If a carcass falls on any seeds that are to be planted, they remain clean.
NIV.38: But if water has been put on the seed and a carcass falls on it, it is unclean for you.
NIV.39: “‘If an animal that you are allowed to eat dies, anyone who touches the carcass will be unclean till evening.
NIV.40: Anyone who eats some of the carcass must wash his clothes, and he will be unclean till evening. Anyone who picks up the carcass must wash his clothes, and he will be unclean till evening.
NIV.41: “‘Every creature that moves about on the ground is detestable; it is not to be eaten.
NIV.42: You are not to eat any creature that moves about on the ground, whether it moves on its belly or walks on all fours or on many feet; it is detestable.
NIV.43: Do not defile yourselves by any of these creatures. Do not make yourselves unclean by means of them or be made unclean by them.
NIV.44: I am the Lord your God; consecrate yourselves and be holy, because I am holy. Do not make yourselves unclean by any creature that moves about on the ground.
NIV.45: I am the Lord who brought you up out of Egypt to be your God; therefore be holy, because I am holy.
NIV.46: “‘These are the regulations concerning animals, birds, every living thing that moves in the water and every creature that moves about on the ground.
NIV.47: You must distinguish between the unclean and the clean, between living creatures that may be eaten and those that may not be eaten.’”

NRSVCE.1: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying to them:
NRSVCE.2: Speak to the people of Israel, saying: From among all the land animals, these are the creatures that you may eat.
NRSVCE.3: Any animal that has divided hoofs and is cleft-footed and chews the cud — such you may eat.
NRSVCE.4: But among those that chew the cud or have divided hoofs, you shall not eat the following: the camel, for even though it chews the cud, it does not have divided hoofs; it is unclean for you.
NRSVCE.5: The rock badger, for even though it chews the cud, it does not have divided hoofs; it is unclean for you.
NRSVCE.6: The hare, for even though it chews the cud, it does not have divided hoofs; it is unclean for you.
NRSVCE.7: The pig, for even though it has divided hoofs and is cleft-footed, it does not chew the cud; it is unclean for you.
NRSVCE.8: Of their flesh you shall not eat, and their carcasses you shall not touch; they are unclean for you.
NRSVCE.9: These you may eat, of all that are in the waters. Everything in the waters that has fins and scales, whether in the seas or in the streams — such you may eat.
NRSVCE.10: But anything in the seas or the streams that does not have fins and scales, of the swarming creatures in the waters and among all the other living creatures that are in the waters — they are detestable to you
NRSVCE.11: and detestable they shall remain. Of their flesh you shall not eat, and their carcasses you shall regard as detestable.
NRSVCE.12: Everything in the waters that does not have fins and scales is detestable to you.
NRSVCE.13: These you shall regard as detestable among the birds. They shall not be eaten; they are an abomination: the eagle, the vulture, the osprey,
NRSVCE.14: the buzzard, the kite of any kind;
NRSVCE.16: the ostrich, the nighthawk, the sea gull, the hawk of any kind;
NRSVCE.17: the little owl, the cormorant, the great owl,
NRSVCE.18: the water hen, the desert owl, the carrion vulture,
NRSVCE.19: the stork, the heron of any kind, the hoopoe, and the bat.
NRSVCE.20: All winged insects that walk upon all fours are detestable to you.
NRSVCE.21: But among the winged insects that walk on all fours you may eat those that have jointed legs above their feet, with which to leap on the ground.
NRSVCE.22: Of them you may eat: the locust according to its kind, the bald locust according to its kind, the cricket according to its kind, and the grasshopper according to its kind.
NRSVCE.23: But all other winged insects that have four feet are detestable to you.
NRSVCE.24: By these you shall become unclean; whoever touches the carcass of any of them shall be unclean until the evening,
NRSVCE.25: and whoever carries any part of the carcass of any of them shall wash his clothes and be unclean until the evening.
NRSVCE.26: Every animal that has divided hoofs but is not cleft-footed or does not chew the cud is unclean for you; everyone who touches one of them shall be unclean.
NRSVCE.27: All that walk on their paws, among the animals that walk on all fours, are unclean for you; whoever touches the carcass of any of them shall be unclean until the evening,
NRSVCE.28: and the one who carries the carcass shall wash his clothes and be unclean until the evening; they are unclean for you.
NRSVCE.29: These are unclean for you among the creatures that swarm upon the earth: the weasel, the mouse, the great lizard according to its kind,
NRSVCE.30: the gecko, the land crocodile, the lizard, the sand lizard, and the chameleon.
NRSVCE.31: These are unclean for you among all that swarm; whoever touches one of them when they are dead shall be unclean until the evening.
NRSVCE.32: And anything upon which any of them falls when they are dead shall be unclean, whether an article of wood or cloth or skin or sacking, any article that is used for any purpose; it shall be dipped into water, and it shall be unclean until the evening, and then it shall be clean.
NRSVCE.33: And if any of them falls into any earthen vessel, all that is in it shall be unclean, and you shall break the vessel.
NRSVCE.34: Any food that could be eaten shall be unclean if water from any such vessel comes upon it; and any liquid that could be drunk shall be unclean if it was in any such vessel.
NRSVCE.35: Everything on which any part of the carcass falls shall be unclean; whether an oven or stove, it shall be broken in pieces; they are unclean, and shall remain unclean for you.
NRSVCE.36: But a spring or a cistern holding water shall be clean, while whatever touches the carcass in it shall be unclean.
NRSVCE.37: If any part of their carcass falls upon any seed set aside for sowing, it is clean;
NRSVCE.38: but if water is put on the seed and any part of their carcass falls on it, it is unclean for you.
NRSVCE.39: If an animal of which you may eat dies, anyone who touches its carcass shall be unclean until the evening.
NRSVCE.40: Those who eat of its carcass shall wash their clothes and be unclean until the evening; and those who carry the carcass shall wash their clothes and be unclean until the evening.
NRSVCE.41: All creatures that swarm upon the earth are detestable; they shall not be eaten.
NRSVCE.42: Whatever moves on its belly, and whatever moves on all fours, or whatever has many feet, all the creatures that swarm upon the earth, you shall not eat; for they are detestable.
NRSVCE.43: You shall not make yourselves detestable with any creature that swarms; you shall not defile yourselves with them, and so become unclean.
NRSVCE.44: For I am the LORD your God; sanctify yourselves therefore, and be holy, for I am holy. You shall not defile yourselves with any swarming creature that moves on the earth.
NRSVCE.45: For I am the LORD who brought you up from the land of Egypt, to be your God; you shall be holy, for I am holy.
NRSVCE.46: This is the law pertaining to land animal and bird and every living creature that moves through the waters and every creature that swarms upon the earth,
NRSVCE.47: to make a distinction between the unclean and the clean, and between the living creature that may be eaten and the living creature that may not be eaten.

NET.1: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying to them,
NET.2: “Tell the Israelites: ‘This is the kind of creature you may eat from among all the animals that are on the land.
NET.3: You may eat any among the animals that has a divided hoof (the hooves are completely split in two ) and that also chews the cud.
NET.4: However, you must not eat these from among those that chew the cud and have divided hooves: The camel is unclean to you because it chews the cud even though its hoof is not divided.
NET.5: The rock badger is unclean to you because it chews the cud even though its hoof is not divided.
NET.6: The hare is unclean to you because it chews the cud even though its hoof is not divided.
NET.7: The pig is unclean to you because its hoof is divided (the hoof is completely split in two ), even though it does not chew the cud.
NET.8: You must not eat from their meat and you must not touch their carcasses; they are unclean to you.
NET.9: “‘These you can eat from all creatures that are in the water: Any creatures in the water that have both fins and scales, whether in the seas or in the streams, you may eat.
NET.10: But any creatures that do not have both fins and scales, whether in the seas or in the streams, from all the swarming things of the water and from all the living creatures that are in the water, are detestable to you.
NET.11: Since they are detestable to you, you must not eat their meat and their carcass you must detest.
NET.12: Any creature in the water that does not have both fins and scales is detestable to you.
NET.13: “‘These you are to detest from among the birds — they must not be eaten, because they are detestable: the griffon vulture, the bearded vulture, the black vulture,
NET.14: the kite, the buzzard of any kind,
NET.16: the eagle owl, the short-eared owl, the long-eared owl, the hawk of any kind,
NET.17: the little owl, the cormorant, the screech owl,
NET.18: the white owl, the scops owl, the osprey,
NET.19: the stork, the heron of any kind, the hoopoe, and the bat.
NET.20: “‘Every winged swarming thing that walks on all fours is detestable to you.
NET.21: However, this you may eat from all the winged swarming things that walk on all fours, which have jointed legs to hop with on the land.
NET.22: These you may eat from them: the locust of any kind, the bald locust of any kind, the cricket of any kind, the grasshopper of any kind.
NET.23: But any other winged swarming thing that has four legs is detestable to you.
NET.24: “‘By these you defile yourselves; anyone who touches their carcass will be unclean until the evening,
NET.25: and anyone who carries their carcass must wash his clothes and will be unclean until the evening.
NET.26: “‘All animals that divide the hoof but it is not completely split in two and do not chew the cud are unclean to you; anyone who touches them becomes unclean.
NET.27: All that walk on their paws among all the creatures that walk on all fours are unclean to you. Anyone who touches their carcass will be unclean until the evening,
NET.28: and the one who carries their carcass must wash his clothes and be unclean until the evening; they are unclean to you.
NET.29: “‘Now this is what is unclean to you among the swarming things that swarm on the land: the rat, the mouse, the large lizard of any kind,
NET.30: the Mediterranean gecko, the spotted lizard, the wall gecko, the skink, and the chameleon.
NET.31: These are the ones that are unclean to you among all the swarming things. Anyone who touches them when they die will be unclean until evening.
NET.32: Also, anything they fall on when they die will become unclean — any wood vessel or garment or article of leather or sackcloth. Any such vessel with which work is done must be immersed in water and will be unclean until the evening. Then it will become clean.
NET.33: As for any clay vessel they fall into, everything in it will become unclean and you must break it.
NET.34: Any food that may be eaten which becomes soaked with water will become unclean. Anything drinkable in any such vessel will become unclean.
NET.35: Anything their carcass may fall on will become unclean. An oven or small stove must be smashed to pieces; they are unclean, and they will stay unclean to you.
NET.36: However, a spring or a cistern which collects water will be clean, but one who touches their carcass will be unclean.
NET.37: Now, if such a carcass falls on any sowing seed which is to be sown, it is clean,
NET.38: but if water is put on the seed and such a carcass falls on it, it is unclean to you.
NET.39: “‘Now if an animal that you may eat dies, whoever touches its carcass will be unclean until the evening.
NET.40: One who eats from its carcass must wash his clothes and be unclean until the evening, and whoever carries its carcass must wash his clothes and be unclean until the evening.
NET.41: Every swarming thing that swarms on the land is detestable; it must not be eaten.
NET.42: You must not eat anything that crawls on its belly or anything that walks on all fours or on any number of legs of all the swarming things that swarm on the land, because they are detestable.
NET.43: Do not make yourselves detestable by any of the swarming things. You must not defile yourselves by them and become unclean by them,
NET.44: for I am the LORD your God and you are to sanctify yourselves and be holy because I am holy. You must not defile yourselves by any of the swarming things that creep on the ground,
NET.45: for I am the LORD who brought you up from the land of Egypt to be your God, and you are to be holy because I am holy.
NET.46: This is the law of the land animals, the birds, all the living creatures that move in the water, and all the creatures that swarm on the land,
NET.47: to distinguish between the unclean and the clean, between the living creatures that may be eaten and the living creatures that must not be eaten.’”
